text:
Alex Vlasic grew up a few miles from the United Center, and he has become the defenseman Chicago hands the hardest job. He played 28.5 minutes in Calgary on Saturday, and his ice time is up almost three minutes a night over his last ten games, to 23. Evolving-Hockey ranked his competition in the 99th percentile last season.

The results reflect that job and the team around him. The Blackhawks get only about 41% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, and he has no goals and five assists in 23 games. Evolving-Hockey also notes he played with some of the weakest teammates in the league last season (bottom 2% by their impact), which drags his raw numbers down more than his own play does.

The weak spot is the first pass. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him keeping possession on only 31% of his exits last season, so watch for clears off the glass when a team forechecks hard. He isn't a scorer, and our range sees around 22 points. What Chicago needs from him is fewer shifts spent pinned in his own end.
